lines.speaker: Nour
lines.text: Okay, so I just got off the phone with the client, and they're moving the demo up to tomorrow morning. Eight a.m. sharp.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Tomorrow? Nour, come on. That's not funny.

lines.speaker: Nour
lines.text: I'm not laughing, Tarek. Eight a.m. They confirmed it twice.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: But the pipeline's still failing on the third stage. We haven't even—

lines.speaker: Nour
lines.text: I know. I know exactly where we are. That's why I called this meeting.

lines.speaker: Qureshi
lines.text: Let her finish, Tarek. Go on, Nour.

lines.speaker: Nour
lines.text: Thank you. Look, the data migration is done. The auth layer is solid. It's just the transcription stage that keeps choking.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Choking? It's not choking, it's dying. It dies every single time we push more than forty seconds of audio.

lines.speaker: Qureshi
lines.text: Forty seconds. That's a hard limit, or is it a timing issue?

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Honestly? We don't know yet. It could be memory. It could be the model weights loading twice. It could be—

lines.speaker: Nour
lines.text: It's the weights. I checked the logs at two this morning. It's loading the model twice on the second worker.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Wait— seriously? You found that at two a.m. and you didn't wake me?

lines.speaker: Nour
lines.text: You were asleep, Tarek. You needed it. And I wasn't sure yet.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: I don't need sleep, I need— okay. Okay, fine. So it's a config bug. That's fixable. That's actually fixable.

lines.speaker: Qureshi
lines.text: How long to fix it, and how long to verify it?

lines.speaker: Nour
lines.text: The fix itself? Twenty minutes. Verifying it against the full test set—that’s where things go sideways.

lines.speaker: Qureshi
lines.text: How long?

lines.speaker: Nour
lines.text: Four hours. Maybe five if the cache is cold.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Five hours. It's nine p.m. now. That puts us at two, maybe three in the morning.

lines.speaker: Qureshi
lines.text: Then we start now and we don't stop until it's green.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Qureshi, c’mon—the team’s been grinding since seven. They’re running on fumes.

lines.speaker: Qureshi
lines.text: I'm not asking the whole team. I'm asking the three of us. And I'll be in the room the entire time.

lines.speaker: Nour
lines.text: He's right. If we hand this off half-fixed and it breaks on stage tomorrow, we don't get a second demo.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Fine. Fine. But I'm ordering food first. Real food. Not the vending machine stuff.

lines.speaker: Nour
lines.text: Deal. Get the biryani place on Clement.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: The one with the— oh, that one. Yeah. Okay. Extra raita?

lines.speaker: Nour
lines.text: Obviously extra raita. Who raised you?

lines.speaker: Qureshi
lines.text: While you two negotiate dinner, I'll pull the staging logs from last night. Nour, send me the worker config.

lines.speaker: Nour
lines.text: Sending now. And Tarek—

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Yeah?

lines.speaker: Nour
lines.text: I'm sorry I didn't wake you. I should have.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: No, you shouldn't have. You were right. I would've panicked and made it worse.

lines.speaker: Qureshi
lines.text: That’s the realest thing I’ve heard outta either of you all week.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Hey—

lines.speaker: Qureshi
lines.text: I'm not insulting you. I'm saying you're both learning. That's good. Now, the config.

lines.speaker: Nour
lines.text: Sent. Check your inbox.

lines.speaker: Qureshi
lines.text: Got it. Hm. There it is. Two model initializations on worker two. You were right, Nour.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: So we just delete the duplicate call?

lines.speaker: Qureshi
lines.text: Not quite. We need to know why it's being called twice. If we just delete it, it might come back.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Ugh. Of course. Nothing's ever simple.

lines.speaker: Nour
lines.text: Nothing's ever simple, and the demo is in eleven hours. Let's move.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Okay, I'm on the duplicate init. Nour, you take the test harness. Qureshi, you—

lines.speaker: Qureshi
lines.text: I'll watch the logs and keep the client calm if they call. Which they will.

lines.speaker: Nour
lines.text: They always call right when your coffee spills.

lines.speaker: Qureshi
lines.text: That's why I'm here. Go.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Alright. Let's save this thing.

lines.speaker: Nour
lines.text: Wait— Tarek, hold on. Don't touch worker two yet.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Why? It's a duplicate, it's waste, I'm killing it.

lines.speaker: Nour
lines.text: Because if worker one is the one loading it and worker two is just echoing the call, killing it fixes nothing. Check the init sequence first.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Fine, fine— pulling the sequence now. Give me ten seconds.

lines.speaker: Qureshi
lines.text: Ten seconds is generous. I count eight.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: That's it. Worker one is fine. Worker two is fine. It's the scheduler firing both at the same time because the health check times out at three seconds.

lines.speaker: Nour
lines.text: Three seconds? That's—

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Ridiculous, I know. Someone set it in the dev config and it never got changed.

lines.speaker: Qureshi
lines.text: So the fix is a single number.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: A single number. After eleven hours of panic, it's one number.

lines.speaker: Nour
lines.text: I could hug you right now.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Please don't. I haven't eaten since noon.

lines.speaker: Qureshi
lines.text: Change it. Run the test. I'll tell the client we're still on track.

lines.speaker: Nour
lines.text: On track. Try saying that without flinching.

lines.speaker: Qureshi
lines.text: I've said worse with a straighter face.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Qureshi, I swear—

lines.speaker: Qureshi
lines.text: —swear what? That you'll name your firstborn after me? Save it, Tarek. Just run the test.

lines.speaker: Tarek
lines.text: Fine. But if this works, I'm billing the client for emotional damages.

lines.speaker: Nour
lines.text: And dinner. He's billing them for dinner too.

lines.speaker: Qureshi
lines.text: Done. Now everyone stop talking before I remember I hired you.
